facts.text: Luke earned its name when Scottish papermaker William Luke bought the sawmill site in 1881 and renamed the town after himself around 1900.
The town’s economy grew around the Piedmont Pulp and Paper Company, which began operations in 1888 and employed about 1,000 people by 1909.
Luke sits on the north bank of the North Branch Potomac River, just 23 miles southwest of Cumberland, right on the Maryland–West Virginia border.
Before the mill, the area was a company town called West Piedmont built around a sawmill started by Henry Gassaway Davis in 1872 to supply railroad ties.
Verso shut down the Luke paper mill on June 30, 2019, ending more than a century of paper production in the town.
The Devon Club, opened in 1911, served as a social hub for mill workers, offering billiards, bowling, and a library until the 1950s.
